newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures surge to new contract highs.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures surge to new contract highs.

text.p: German Bunds and futures surged to new contract highs in late dealings, buoyed by a firmer U.S. debt market and buying spurred by the Federal Reserve not raising short-term interest rates.
At 1510 GMT, DTB December Bund futures were up 47 basis points at 98.67 and just off the new contract high set at 98.70 when the contract broke support at 98.36 and drew in buyers.
"This has been a day that a lot of people had expected," said one trader. "If the U.S. did not do anything with rates, then the German market was going to head higher."
But some traders doubted how long the euphoria would last.
"I suspect it was a lot of intraday trading and we could be hit by some profit-taking," a trader said. "The economic fundamentals in Germany have not changed to justify the gains."
Dealings on Thursday will focus on the expected release of the 1996 fourth quarter federal debt issuance calendar and supply flowing into the market.
In addition, technical factors will dominate dealings as December Bunds seek to reach resistance at 98.85 amid hopes support holds at 98.16 and 98.00 on any selling bouts.
